findings.title: req.destroy() right after 413 tears down the socket before the response flushes
findings.evidence: After queueing the error response the handler immediately destroys the request; IncomingMessage.destroy() destroys the underlying socket, so the 413 body is often never delivered.
findings.recommendation: Do not kill the socket synchronously in the data handler. Either pause/drain instead of destroying (req.pause() plus res.status(413).set('Connection', 'close')).json(...) and destroy only after res 'finish'/'close': res.on('finish', () => req.destroy()) — or use req.unpipe()/req.resume() to drain so the 413 is flushed first. Add a test asserting the client actually receives 413 for an oversize body.

findings.title: Top-level JSON scalars accepted, so req.body can be null/number/string
findings.evidence: Empty and whitespace-only bodies are normalised to {}, but any valid JSON value is assigned directly, so a body of 'null' yields req.body === null and any handler doing req.body.x throws a TypeError (500).
findings.recommendation: Mirror express.json strict mode: after parsing, reject with 400 when the value is not a non-null object (optionally arrays only), e.g. if (parsed === null || typeof parsed !== 'object') return res.status(400).json(...). Cover 'null', '5' and '"s"' bodies in tests.

findings.title: Chunk size accounting and Buffer.concat assume Buffer chunks
findings.evidence: The comment claims bytes, which is only true for Buffer chunks; if any earlier middleware called req.setEncoding() the chunks are strings, so the cap counts characters (multi-byte bodies bypass the 100_000 byte limit) and Buffer.concat(chunks) in the end handler throws an uncaught TypeError.
findings.evidence_quote: received += chunk.length; // Buffer length: bytes, not characters
findings.recommendation: Normalise chunks (Buffer.isBuffer(chunk) ? chunk : Buffer.from(chunk, 'utf8')) before measuring/pushing, and wrap Buffer.concat in the end handler's try/catch so a decode failure becomes a 400 rather than an unhandled throw. Alternatively call req.setEncoding(null) defensively at entry.

findings.title: No tests around the byte cap and error paths
findings.evidence: The change adds a 100KB cap, 413/415/400 branches and a settled-state race guard, but no test files were added or run, so the boundary (exactly 100_000 vs 100_001) and the response-flush behaviour are unverified.
findings.recommendation: Add tests for: body exactly at the limit (accepted), one byte over (413 actually received by client), content-type gate (415), invalid JSON (400), empty body ({}), and chunked multi-byte UTF-8 split across data events.
